I love that Zappa was willing to take chances and try new things. But, man... Some of his music is pretty shitty. The guitar work is usually pretty great - but the result isn't impressive. When he nailed it, he got it right.

I remember reading about him composing classical music back in high school and it was that aspect that made me really look into composition. Every guitarist has composed something, that's just reality. However, I'd have not composed nearly as much had it not been for reading about him. At the time, I was playing classical guitar - almost exclusively. Realizing that I could compose in the classical style really influenced my musical directions in life.

Granted, I realized that doesn't pay very well - and have largely ceased composition, but I can attribute my compositions to him, at least in part. The Quintessential 80s Song that I banged out? Yup... That can trace its lineage to Zappa - at least in part. It was he who got me interested in it.

And that's the thing about Zappa... He was just so much. He was larger than life. Zappa was full of stories and there's just so much to him that I was unable to actually write about most of it. Zappa was just too much to fit into a single article.

Someday, I may revisit that one and write a smaller series just about him. I've pondered doing that for a few artists on the list - going into more details and discussing their work even more thoroughly. As near as I can tell, there's no end to possible things for me to write about.
